ARCHITECTURE sits at the intersection of four domains:

  ART:
  +------------+
  | proportion |
  | light      |
  | beauty     |
  | meaning    |
  +------------+

  ENGINEERING:
  +--------------+
  | structure    |
  | thermal      |
  | acoustics    |
  | fire/safety  |
  +--------------+

  SOCIAL SCIENCE:
  +----------+
  | behavior |
  | culture  |
  | use      |
  | equity   |
  +----------+

  ECONOMICS:
  +--------------+
  | budget       |
  | schedule     |
  | ROI          |
  | real estate  |
  +--------------+

  None of these alone makes architecture.
  All four simultaneously is the architect's job.

COST RANGE (US construction, 2024)
  ===================================

  Garden shed             $50–100/sqft
  Single-family house     $200–500/sqft     (2,000 sqft = $500K)
  Mid-rise office         $250–450/sqft     (100,000 sqft = $35M)
  Hospital / medical      $1,000–2,500/sqft (500,000 sqft = $750M+)
  Laboratory / cleanroom  $1,500–5,000/sqft
  Data center             $10M–500M+        (power density determines cost)
  Performing arts center  $800–2,000/sqft   (acoustic spec drives cost)

  SERVICE LIFE
  ============
  Wood-frame residential     40–60 years
  Commercial steel/concrete  50–80 years
  Institutional / civic      75–150 years
  Historic / monumental      200–1,000+ years

  THE COST OF LATE DECISIONS
  ==========================
  Decision made in Programming     →  costs 1x to change
  Decision made in Schematic       →  costs 5–10x to change
  Decision made in Design Dev.     →  costs 20–50x to change
  Decision made in CDs             →  costs 100–200x to change
  Change made in construction      →  costs 500–1,000x+ (RFI + delay)

  This is the Boehm curve — same as software.
  Front-load the design, not the documentation.

+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                  WHAT ARCHITECTURE IS NOT                        |
|                                                                  |
|  INTERIOR DESIGN          STRUCTURAL ENGINEERING                 |
|  ----------------         -----------------------                |
|  Finishes, furniture,     Calculates member sizes,               |
|  FF&E, space planning     foundation loads, connection           |
|  within existing shell.   details. PE-licensed.                  |
|  Some states protect      Signs and seals structural             |
|  "interior architect"     drawings. Different exam               |
|  title separately.        (PE, not ARE).                         |
|                                                                  |
|  CONSTRUCTION MGMT        URBAN PLANNING                         |
|  ----------------         ---------------                        |
|  Schedule, budget,        Land use, zoning, transportation,      |
|  subcontractor mgmt,      policy. AICP-certified.                |
|  RFI/submittal            City scale, not building scale.        |
|  processing.              Works in municipalities,               |
|  GC or CM firm role.      not design offices.                    |
|                                                                  |
|  MEP ENGINEERING          ARCHITECTURE-HISTORY                   |
|  ----------------         ---------------------                  |
|  Mechanical, electrical,  Documents, analyzes, critiques         |
|  plumbing, fire.          past buildings. Informs design         |
|  PE-licensed.             precedent but is not design            |
|  (see 04-BUILDING-        practice. (see architecture-           |
|  SYSTEMS.md)              history/ directory)                    |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+

  Architecture is the INTEGRATING discipline.
  The architect sets geometry, intent, and integration.
  Every other consultant works within that framework.

00-OVERVIEW.md          ← You are here
  Architecture as discipline, Vitruvius triad, actors,
  licensure, scale, software parallel.

  01-SPATIAL-DESIGN.md
  Space as primary medium. Programming, adjacency, circulation,
  proportion systems, environmental psychology, Lynch imageability.

  02-STRUCTURAL-LOGIC.md
  Load paths, spanning systems, material behavior, lateral forces,
  structural expression. Data center structural context.

  03-ENVIRONMENTAL.md
  Passive design, daylighting, acoustics, energy modeling,
  Passivhaus, LEED/BREEAM/WELL, embodied carbon.

  04-BUILDING-SYSTEMS.md
  MEP integration, structural grids, facade systems,
  fire protection, BAS, BIM coordination.

  05-DESIGN-PROCESS.md
  AIA phases, BIM/Revit/IFC, parametric design,
  delivery methods, construction documents as specification.

  06-CONTEMPORARY-MOVEMENTS.md
  Parametric/computational, mass timber, biomimicry,
  adaptive reuse, prefabrication, biophilic design.

  07-URBAN-ARCHITECTURE.md
  Urban typologies, ground-floor activation, public space,
  TOD, climate resilience, tall buildings.
